title: Music Basics
description: Notes, instruments, composers and the building blocks of music

questions.question: How many lines are on a standard musical staff?
questions.explanation: A staff has five lines and four spaces. Notes are placed on them to show pitch.

questions.question: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
questions.explanation: A full-size piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

questions.question: In standard 4/4 time, how many beats does a whole note last?
questions.explanation: A whole note lasts four beats in 4/4. A half note lasts two and a quarter note one.

questions.question: Which instrument family does the trumpet belong to?
questions.explanation: Trumpets are brass instruments: the player buzzes their lips into a cup-shaped mouthpiece.

questions.question: Which composer wrote the 'Moonlight Sonata' and continued composing after losing his hearing?
questions.explanation: Beethoven wrote the 'Moonlight Sonata' in 1801. He was almost completely deaf when he composed his Ninth Symphony.

questions.question: What does 'forte' mean in sheet music?
questions.explanation: 'Forte' (f) means loud and 'piano' (p) means soft. Tempo terms like 'allegro' (fast) are separate.

questions.question: How many notes are in a standard major scale, not counting the repeated top note?
questions.explanation: A major scale has seven distinct notes, such as C D E F G A B, before returning to C an octave higher.

questions.question: Which note is a perfect fifth above C?
questions.explanation: Counting C, D, E, F, G gives five letter names, and C to G is a perfect fifth (seven semitones).

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.explanation: A standard guitar has six strings, usually tuned E A D G B E. Twelve-string guitars exist but are less common.

questions.question: Which composer wrote 'The Four Seasons' violin concertos?
questions.explanation: Antonio Vivaldi published 'The Four Seasons' in 1725. Each concerto depicts a season of the year.
